questions.question: Which town or city do you live in now?

segments.v: I live in Hà Nội, the capital of Vietnam. I live in Cầu Giấy district with my family. It is a big and busy city.
I live in Hà Nội — Cầu Giấy
side of the city. I've lived there pretty much my whole life, so it's
a bit of a concrete jungle
my school, my friends, and the best street food I know.

fluency.band6: Three short sentences with no linking words; the answer stops after the basic facts.
fluency.band9: Direct answer, then narrows (“to be exact”), adds a personal link (“so”), and balances a negative with a positive (“to be honest… but”). Ends with a list after a colon.

lexical.band6: General words (“big”, “busy city”); “I live” is repeated.
lexical.band9: Idiomatic and precise: home turf, a bit of a concrete jungle, where everything happens. “A bit of” softens the criticism.

grammar.band6: Only “I live…” and “It is…”: accurate but a narrow range.
grammar.band9: Present perfect for duration (I've lived there pretty much my whole life); result clause with “so”; noun clause (where everything happens); superlative + reduced relative (the best street food I know).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 lists three flat facts with repeated “I live… It is…”. Band 9 narrows the location, adds a personal connection, and gives a balanced view (negative + positive) using natural idioms.

vocabulary.definition: the centre of activity in a place

fluency.band6: “Yes, there are” then a list; “also” is the only linking word.
fluency.band9: “Yeah, a couple” signals how many problems; “The main one is…” organises the answer; “too” adds a second point; a vivid example closes it.

lexical.band9: Topic-specific collocations: rush hour, a sea of motorbikes, drag on, air quality, smog, leave a lot to be desired.

grammar.band9: Prepositional time phrase (During rush hour), modal (can easily drag on), “when” clause, and the “so… that” result structure (so thick you can barely see).

questions.question: Do you think you will continue to live there for a long time? (Why? Why not?)

segments.v: I think no. After I finish high school, I want to study abroad. Maybe I will come back later.
for a few years and see how people live somewhere else. That said, all my family is here, so I can

fluency.band6: Clear but abrupt; the last sentence (“Maybe I will come back later”) is not developed.
fluency.band9: Hedge → condition → purpose → contrast (“That said”) → final prediction. Each idea leads to the next.

lexical.band6: Adequate but basic: study abroad, come back.
lexical.band9: for good, spread my wings, overseas, settle back, eventually.

grammar.band6: Error: “I think no” (correct: “I don't think so”). Only “want” and “will”.
grammar.band9: Conditional with a fixed phrase (If everything goes to plan, I'll…), “I'd like to”, and “can see myself + V-ing”.

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 has an error: “I think no” should be “I don't think so”. Band 9 answers with a hedge (“probably not”), gives a condition, and adds a contrast with “That said”.

fluency.band6: Lists changes but never explains their effect on people.
fluency.band9: “The biggest one is…” ranks the changes; “so” gives a consequence; “Also” adds a second change with its own effect.

lexical.band9: Precise: elevated section, runs right through, battling the traffic, low-rise, torn down, make way for, skyline.

and more about the people. We always sit down to dinner together, even when everyone's
